To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relationship between art practices and citizenship are best placed in a localized (avant gar de) context that is self sufficient and heterogeneous.

the relationship between art, citizenship and democracy can be best articulated through the practice of the artist citizen, who is able to demonstrate an effective relationship through the articulation and demonstration of an avant garde localized (micro) politics.
a 'localized' practice is the best place for an effective relationship between an artist citizen and citizenship, which is best placed in the context of an agonistic, self sustaining micropolitic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between art, citizenship and a micro politic.
the question of what the relationship is between art practice and citizen ship.
the role of art practice as a site of resistance to the colonization of citizenship by the neo liberal politics of globalization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between art, citizenship and democracy is a complex and difficult one to negotiate, and that the research presented here is only a starting point for further investigation.
art practice and citizenship are not mutually exclusive.
this research demonstrates a relationship between art practice as the avant garde and citizenship, which can be best described as a 'localized' and self sufficient micro politic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thesis has provided an understanding of the relationship between the art practice and citizenship through an analysis of the work of Atelier van Lieshou, Nicolas Bourriaud and Documenta 11.
we have developed a new approach to art making and art education that has been informed by our own practice, research and teaching.

we have attempted to create a space in which the relationship between art, citizenship and the avant garde is not a relationship that is defined by a liberal politics of the avant garde as a universalist, international canon, or by a neo liberal politics of the art market as a universalist international canon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between art, citizenship and democracy is not an abstract concept, but is a lived and embodied reality.
art can be used as a tool for social change.
we are not just artists.
